gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a single accuracy yardstick (passing the ISO 81060-2 clinical validation) only the Huawei Watch D2 among the cards passes for the general population, while the newer Watch D3 it recommended has not been validated yet (Fnac measured it 7/6 mmHg below an Omron cuff), and the 'FDA-cleared' Omron HeartGuide is discontinued and has a second model code (HEM-6411T-ZM) with no published validation.
standout_why: I compared this against these pages: the FDA safety notice (cited) names no products. The Hilo blog (cited) gives no mean ± SD, no ISO 81060-2 result and no 510(k) number for any band. Fitcoin (rank 13, not cited) has a table with method, regulator and calibration interval, but it lists the D3 only as 'CE-MDR medical device' with 'None stated' for accuracy, gives no wrist ranges, and says nothing about the D2 or Omron. SamMobile (not cited) covers only Samsung's wellness status. The HeartGuide gets one card but no page in the results checks its status. I could not open three pages: Wareable's D3 review (403), Android Authority (403) and Cardilog (certificate error). The Wareable review is cited and may discuss D3 validation, which is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: It moves the cuff pick from the Watch D3 to the Watch D2. The D2 is the only cuff watch on offer with a pass under ISO 81060-2 (85-subject primary study plus stress and ambulatory studies). The D3 has no validation yet, and a named reviewer measured it outside the 5 mmHg mean-error bound. It also takes the Omron HeartGuide out of the 'medical-focused' slot: Medaval lists it as discontinued, and the clearance (K182481) covers the HEM-6410T-ZM, so the HEM-6411T-ZM code is not a validated buy. Samsung, Hilo Core and Apple stay as trend or notification tools. Samsung and Hilo call their products wellness features, and neither publishes a validation result for its estimates.

findings.label: Clinical validation (normalised yardstick: ISO 81060-2)
findings.value: Pass, general population, ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd 1:2020/Amd 2:2024: primary 85-subject study, stress study (n=35), ambulatory study (n=35); Medaval rates it 3 stars
findings.note: Model LCA-B11. The page gives no mean ± SD. ISO 81060-2 passes require a mean difference within ±5 mmHg and SD ≤ 8 mmHg against a reference.

findings.label: Clinical validation status
findings.value: Not yet validated to AAMI/ESH/ISO (the D2 is)
findings.source_title: Test Huawei Watch D3 | L'Éclaireur Fnac (Sofian Nouira, 2026-10-06)
findings.note: Quote: 'La D3 n'a pas encore fait l'objet d'une telle validation.' I found no Medaval entry for the D3.

findings.label: Reviewer-measured offset vs upper-arm cuff
findings.value: Average 7 mmHg lower systolic and 6 mmHg lower diastolic than an Omron M3 Comfort
findings.source_title: Test Huawei Watch D3 | L'Éclaireur Fnac (Sofian Nouira, 2026-10-06)
findings.note: Measured by Sofian Nouira at Fnac. He judges it outside the medical standard's 5 mmHg mean-difference limit. This is a single tester's comparison, not a protocol study.

findings.label: Wrist range per cuff strap
findings.source_title: Test Huawei Watch D3 | L'Éclaireur Fnac
findings.note: Both sizes come in the box, per the review.

findings.label: Wrist range per airbag strap
findings.value: M: 130–160 mm; L: 161–210 mm (130–210 mm overall); both in box

findings.label: Battery life, normalised by BP load
findings.value: Up to 6 days at 6 BP + 5 ECG readings per day; up to 1 day with 24-hour ambulatory BP (ABPM) at 15-minute intervals
findings.note: The headline '6 days' assumes spot checks. Turning on the 24-hour BP feature that ChatGPT's card advertises cuts it to 1 day.

findings.label: FDA clearance: which model code
findings.value: 510(k) K182481, 'HEM-6410T-ZM Wrist Blood Pressure Monitor', product code DXN, SESE decision 11/09/2018
findings.note: DXN is the product code the FDA safety notice tells shoppers to look for.

findings.label: Validation and availability (HEM-6410T-ZM)
findings.value: Pass, ISO 81060-2:2013 general population (Kuwabara et al., J Clin Hypertens 2019); Medaval 2 stars; listed as discontinued but may still be sold, US only
findings.note: Medaval notes that Stride BP does not list it for self-measurement, while the AMA VDL does, citing the published study plus FDA clearance.

findings.label: Validation (HEM-6411T-ZM variant)
findings.value: No peer-reviewed clinical validation; Medaval 'Not recommended'
findings.note: Both codes are sold as 'BP8000-M', so the shopper has to check the HEM code on the box.

findings.label: US regulatory status of BP estimate
findings.value: Wellness feature; Samsung told Android Authority it is 'not subject to FDA clearance'
findings.source_title: Galaxy Watch blood pressure monitoring isn't approved by the US FDA | SamMobile
findings.note: No accuracy or validation figure is published for the US release.

findings.label: What is FDA-cleared
findings.value: Only the Hilo Cuff (upper-arm calibration cuff); 'Hilo Core is a wellness product and is not a medical device'
findings.note: The footnote says the scientific evidence relates to a product using the same cuffless technology. That is the separately 510(k)-cleared Aktiia G0 / Hilo Band, per FierceBiotech (2025-07-08): https://www.fiercebiotech.com/medtech/fda-clears-over-counter-cuffless-blood-pressure-monitor-hilo-bracelet

findings.label: Calibration interval and price
findings.value: Recalibrates every 30 days; up to 35 band measurements/day; US$89.99 hardware + US$149.99/yr = US$239.98 first year
findings.source_title: Blood pressure wearables: Hilo Core vs. HLTH vs. Hume | Hilo
findings.note: From the maker's own comparison page. For comparison, Samsung recalibrates every 28 days according to ChatGPT's answer; I did not verify that.

findings.label: How to check US authorisation
findings.value: Search the FDA 510(k) database by device name; authorised BP devices generally carry product code DXN; the warning applies to wearable features 'regardless of brand'
findings.source_title: Do Not Use Unauthorized Devices for Measuring Blood Pressure: FDA Safety Communication
